notes:
POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity can meet NexGen's clinical triage and document search SLAs and provide predictable cost for reserved GPUs.

Representative workload & targets:
- Workloads: patient triage chat (multi-turn, ~150-300 tokens), EHR summarization (512-1024 tokens), embedding-based doc-search + reranking.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 350ms for chat (up to 256 tokens), p95 < 600ms for 512-token summarization; cold-cache allowed higher during first-minute warm-up.
- Throughput/Capacity ask: sustain 150-200 concurrent chat sessions (avg 2 requests/min per session) and 200 QPS for embedding lookups during peak windows.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; prefers reserved pricing but needs predictable unit economics for budgeting.

POC setup details:
- Cluster: Redwood Dedicated dev cluster provisioned: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (initial), plan to test 8x for production sizing.
- Software: model variant = open-llm-v3-13B-quant (customer preference for open model), quantized execution path enabled, KV cache enabled.
- Routing: single-region (us-east) test with VPC peering to NexGen test environment.

Test plan executed so far:
- Load tests: ramp to 120 QPS steady-state for chat prompts; observed p95=190ms for 256-token chat after warm-up; initial cold-cache p95 spikes to 1.2s for first few seconds.
- Soak tests: 48h run completed with no OOMs; token throughput stable after 6h; observed cache eviction thresholds causing CPU spike on host at hour 30 (investigating).
- Stress tests: short bursts to 220 QPS caused queuing and increased tail latency — indicates need for additional reserved GPUs or autoscale buffer for burst capacity.

Key findings / recommendations:
- Warm-up behavior: KV cache warm-up critical — recommend pre-warming during known peak windows or keep cache warm with synthetic traffic to avoid initial latency spikes.
- Sizing: initial 4x GPU cluster meets baseline but to achieve 200 concurrent chats and headroom for bursts, recommend 8x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs or mixed pool (6 reserved + 2 burstable).
- SLA negotiation points: customer requests 99.99% uptime for Dedicated; Redwood proposed 99.95% with credits. Need to align on incident response times and support hours (NexGen requests 24/7).
- Security: vendor attestation required for data residency (support for on-prem appliance or private control plane). Legal requested explicit KMS integration and audit-log retention windows (7 years).

Open action items / blockers:
- Procurement sign-off for on-prem vs hosted Dedicated — hardware CAPEX approval pending (Finance).
- Legal: finalize data residency clause and SLA penalty language (expected 2–3 weeks).
- Engineering: reproduce CPU spike cause (cache eviction) observed at hour 30 in soak test; SE assigned to run memory profile and propose kernel tuning.

- "If you can guarantee throughput with a clear reserved plan and SLA, procurement will greenlight." — Head of Ops, Marisol Gomez
